en: PHIVOLCS declares a six-kilometer Permanent Danger Zone around Mayon Volcano to protect people from deadly lava flows.
Coastal provinces like Surigao del Sur must prepare for tsunamis because they face the deep Philippine Trench.
The province of Cagayan frequently experiences typhoons because it sits at the northernmost tip of Luzon facing the Pacific.
The Cagayan River often overflows during heavy rains, so residents in Tuguegarao must know their local evacuation routes.
Laguna de Bay's shallow waters can breed mosquitoes if not managed, increasing dengue risk for nearby communities.
Hikers climbing Mount Pulag must bring thick jackets because temperatures at its peak can drop below freezing.
Swimmers at La Union beaches must watch for rip currents, which are strong underwater channels that pull people seaward.
Residents in Batangas must wear N95 masks during Taal Volcano eruptions to prevent inhaling harmful volcanic ash.
Metro Manila experiences higher temperatures than Baguio City because its dense concrete buildings trap heat, requiring frequent hydration.
Residents in mountainous Benguet should avoid building houses on steep slopes to prevent landslide injuries during heavy rains.
The Philippines is close to the equator, so students must apply sunscreen to protect their skin from intense ultraviolet rays.
Wading in untreated floodwater in flood-prone Marikina City can cause leptospirosis, a severe bacterial infection from rat urine.
